entities.name: Greco-Turkish War of 1897
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Greco-Turkish War of 1897 was a pivotal conflict between the kingdom of Greece and the Ottoman Empire, fought on Greek soil between April 18 and May 20, 1897. This war marked a significant turning point in the struggle for Greek independence and sovereignty, as Greece sought to assert its control over the disputed region of Macedonia. The war was sparked by a series of border disputes and skirmishes between Greek and Ottoman forces, which ultimately led to a full-scale conflict. The war ended with the signing of the Treaty of Constantinople on May 20, 1897, which recognized Greek control over the region of Macedonia, but also imposed significant territorial concessions on Greece. 

 The war had a profound impact on the development of modern Greece, as it marked the beginning of a new era of Greek self-determination and sovereignty. The war also had significant regional implications, as it contributed to the eventual collapse of the Ottoman Empire and the subsequent partitioning of its territories. The war also had a lasting impact on the international community, as it highlighted the importance of Greek independence and sovereignty in the modern world. 

 In the words of the Greek historian, Georgios P. Kostakopoulos, 'The Greco-Turkish War of 1897 was a defining moment in the struggle for Greek independence, marking the beginning of a new era of self-determination and sovereignty.'
